originalTitle: VTI’s 3,000 Extra Stocks Cost Holders $393,400 Per $500,000 Over the Past Decade
summary: The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF promises broader diversification than the S&P 500, but a decade of returns tells a different story about what those extra 3,000 tickers actually deliver to your portfolio.
content:
The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF promises broader diversification than the S&P 500, but a decade of returns tells a different story about what those extra 3,000 tickers actually deliver to your portfolio.

The ETF Examiner desk. Editor: Ryne Mauck .

Small-Cap Drag Hiding Inside Your Total Market Fund

If you put $500,000 into the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF ( NYSEARCA:VTI ) ten years ago instead of the S&P 500, the “extra diversification” cost you roughly $393,400 in foregone gains. That gap does not appear anywhere on the marketing sheet next to the ticker.

What “Total Market” Actually Delivered

Over the ten years ending September 21, 2026, VTI returned 243.42% on a price basis, moving from $111.15 to $381.71 per share. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ( NYSEARCA:VOO ) returned 322.10% over the same window, climbing from $168.94 to $713.11 per share. A $500,000 stake in VTI grew to roughly $1,717,100. The same money in VOO grew to about $2,110,500. The 78.68 percentage-point spread is the price of owning “the rest of the market.”

Composition drives this shortfall. VOO charges 0.03% a year, or about $3 per $10,000 invested over twelve months — the same fee tier as VTI. The divergence traces to what each fund actually owns.

Why 3,000 Extra Tickers Quietly Underperformed

VTI’s pitch is breadth: roughly 3,000 small- and mid-cap names that sit outside the S&P 500. Over the past decade, breadth worked against holders. Returns concentrated in the largest US companies. The mega-caps that anchor the S&P 500 pulled away from the long tail of small caps, regional banks, biotechs, and micro-cap issuers that only VTI holds. Those extra tickers diluted holders’ exposure to the winners.

Weighting makes the drag persistent. Both funds are market-cap weighted, so their top holdings look nearly identical. VOO owns 519 stocks concentrated in the largest US firms, with 38.0% in information technology as of June 30, 2026. VTI holds those same mega-caps at similar weights, then adds thousands of smaller issuers that have lagged. You are paying for largely the same big-tech-heavy portfolio, then effectively giving back returns each year to a long tail of underperformers. Ten years of that dilution compounds into a mid-six-figure gap on a half-million-dollar account.

Cheaper-Behaving Mirrors on the Same Shelf

Two obvious alternatives sit right next to VTI. VOO tracks the S&P 500 for the same 0.03% annual fee, with a portfolio turnover rate of just 1%, which limits taxable capital-gains distributions. The iShares Core S&P Total US Stock Market ETF ( NYSEARCA:ITOT ) delivers similar total-market exposure at the same 0.03% fee, so switching to ITOT leaves the same composition drag intact. The Schwab US Broad Market ETF ( NYSEARCA:SCHB ) sits in the same broad-market bucket with a comparable long tail of small caps. The trade-off is real: swapping VTI for VOO strips out roughly 3,000 smaller names, which could hurt performance in cycles where small caps lead.

Questions to Ask Before Your Next Contribution

Are you paying VTI for the small-cap sleeve you actually want, or simply for a “total market” label that has trailed the S&P 500 by 78.68 percentage points over ten years? The fee is trivial. Composition is the hidden cost. A holder who wants pure large-cap exposure has a cheaper-behaving mirror in VOO. A holder who genuinely wants small-cap breadth should size that position knowing it has been a drag on this cycle rather than a diversifier.

chineseTitle: 过去十年，VTI 的 3,000 股额外股票让持有者每持有 500,000 美元就要损失 393,400 美元
chineseSummary: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF 承诺比标准普尔 500 指数更广泛的多元化，但十年的回报却讲述了一个不同的故事，即这额外的 3,000 只股票实际上为您的投资组合带来了什么。
chineseContent:
Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF 承诺比标准普尔 500 指数更广泛的多元化，但十年的回报却讲述了一个不同的故事，即这额外的 3,000 只股票实际上为您的投资组合带来了什么。

ETF 审查员柜台。编辑：莱恩·莫克。

隐藏在整个市场基金中的小盘股拖累

如果您十年前将 500,000 美元投入 Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEARCA:VTI)，而不是标准普尔 500 指数，那么“额外的多元化”会让您损失大约 393,400 美元的收益。该差距不会出现在股票行情表旁边的营销表上的任何位置。

“总市场”实际提供了什么

截至 2026 年 9 月 21 日的十年中，VTI 的价格回报率为 243.42%，从每股 111.15 美元升至 381.71 美元。 Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ( NYSEARCA:VOO ) 在同一时期的回报率为 322.10%，从每股 168.94 美元攀升至 713.11 美元。价值 500,000 美元的 VTI 股份增至约 1,717,100 美元。 VOO 中的同样资金增长至约 2,110,500 美元。 78.68 个百分点的利差是拥有“市场其余部分”的价格。

构成导致了这种短缺。 VOO 每年收取 0.03% 的费用，即 12 个月内每投资 10,000 美元约收取 3 美元——与 VTI 的费用等级相同。这种差异可以追溯到每只基金实际拥有的资产。

为什么 3,000 只额外股票表现悄然不佳

VTI 的宣传重点是广度：标普 500 指数之外的大约 3,000 家中小盘股。在过去十年中，广度对持有者不利。回报集中在美国最大的公司。锚定标准普尔 500 指数的大型股脱离了只有 VTI 持有的小型股、区域银行、生物技术和微型股发行人的长尾。这些额外的股票稀释了持有者对赢家的敞口。

加权使阻力持续存在。两只基金均按市值加权，因此它们的最高持股看起来几乎相同。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，VOO 拥有 519 只股票，集中在美国最大的公司，其中 38.0% 为信息技术股。VTI 以相似的权重持有这些相同的大型股，然后增加了数千家落后的小型发行人。你支付的费用基本上是相同的大型科技股投资组合，然后每年有效地将回报返还给表现不佳的长尾公司。经过十年的稀释，五十万美元的账户上出现了六位数的缺口。

同一架子上的廉价镜子

VTI 旁边有两个明显的替代方案。 VOO 跟踪标准普尔 500 指数，年费相同，为 0.03%，投资组合周转率仅为 1%，这限制了应税资本利得分配。 iShares Core S&P Total US Stock Market ETF ( NYSEARCA:ITOT ) 以相同的 0.03% 费用提供类似的总市场敞口，因此切换到 ITOT 会保持相同的成分拖累完好无损。嘉信美国广泛市场 ETF ( NYSEARCA:SCHB ) 与小盘股的长尾属于同一大市场类别。这种权衡是真实的：将 VTI 换成 VOO 会剔除大约 3,000 个较小的公司，这可能会损害小盘股领先的周期中的表现。

在您下次贡献之前要问的问题

您支付 VTI 的费用是为了购买您真正想要的小盘套，还是只是为了购买十年来落后于标准普尔 500 指数 78.68 个百分点的“整体市场”标签？费用是微不足道的。成分是隐性成本。想要纯粹大盘股敞口的持有者在 VOO 中有一个表现更便宜的镜子。真正想要小盘股的持有者应该调整该头寸，因为他知道它是本轮周期的拖累，而不是多元化的工具。
